preconditions.text: The TrailsIntentEntrypoint contract is deployed with its EIP-712 DOMAIN_SEPARATOR computed once in the constructor from block.chainid and stored as an immutable value.; After deployment, the chain forks or the chain ID changes.; Off-chain signatures are generated on the new chain for the signature-based flows such as depositToIntent and depositToIntentWithPermit.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.
evidence: The `TrailsIntentEntrypoint` contract computes its EIP-712 `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR` once in the constructor and stores it as an immutable value. Because `block.chainid` is read once at deployment, the stored `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR` permanently embeds the original chain ID. If the chain later forks or the chain ID changes, this cached domain separator becomes outdated. As a result, the contract will continue validating signatures against an incorrect chain ID.
This causes all off-chain signatures to become invalid on the new chain, breaking signature-based flows such as `depositToIntent` and `depositToIntentWithPermit`.
Any signature generated on the new chain will not match the original domain separator. This creates a permanent denial-of-service for intent verification on the forked chain.

safety.text: Signature verification should be bound to the current chain ID so EIP-712 signatures remain valid after a chain fork or chain ID change.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.
evidence: DOMAIN_SEPARATOR will be invalid after chain forks
